messages.body:
Paul,

sorry for the hour. two things.

1. Derek Furey has now emailed me three times. The third one is a threat, more or less. I've forwarded them all to Colin. He doesn't know what's on the tape but he knows there's something.

2. I finished the transcript. It's attached, full session, with timecodes. The part that matters starts at 40:52. I've marked the [inaudible] bits honestly; there are four in the section and none of them are load-bearing. I also cut a 3-minute excerpt (40:30–43:40) as its own file so nobody has to sit through the dock-strike stories to get to it. I'll bring it on a drive; I'm not attaching audio.

Has your HRP contact said anything?

w

Wren,

I read the transcript this morning with my coffee and then did not finish the coffee.

My contact in the historical unit has pulled the Mahar file from storage. It is thin. Two interviews with Furey and Doucette in October and November 1971, both giving the same account of dropping her at Barrington and Morris. No search of the Arm was ever done; there was no reason to. Doucette died in 2003 in Sydney. There is a note from 1994 that Bernadette Mahar called every October until she died.

What we have is an uncorroborated statement by a deceased man with dementia. What could corroborate it: the vehicle (a 1968 Pontiac registered to Doucette, if the registration survives), any friend Doucette confided in, and the water itself. A sonar survey of the Arm near the Dingle is not impossible; it is also not something HRP will fund on a transcript. I am working on it.

On Derek Furey: forward me the emails. Do not meet him alone. Keep the excerpt and transcript on a drive that is not in your apartment. I am serious about that last part.

Regards,
Paul Kavanagh

forwarded. and understood about the drive.

she called every october.

w

Wren,

Confirming I have the drive you gave me this afternoon (excerpt WAV, full session WAV, transcript, your session log). It is in my safe. A second copy goes to Det. Cst. Amira Hosseini at HRP Historical Case Unit tomorrow morning with a statement from me and, if you are willing, one from you. She will want to interview you. She is good.

I also want to say something as a person rather than as a consultant. You did not have to do any of this. Most people in your position would have handed the card to the producer and gone home. You listened to an old man say a terrible thing and you carried it for three months so that it would end up in the right hands. That is not nothing. Do not let Derek Furey or his lawyer make you feel like a thief. You are the opposite of that.

Regards,
Paul Kavanagh

thank you. yes to the interview. any day.

I'm going to write to Maureen tonight. I know you said wait for HRP. I've been waiting for three months and she's been waiting for fifty-five years and I don't think I get to add to that.

w

I would have told you not to. I would also have understood. Be gentle with her and with yourself.

PK

Dear Ms. Mahar-Lyle,

My name is Wren Castellanos. I'm a sound recordist in Halifax. I found your name in a 2021 Harbour Ledger article about your mother, Colleen, and I've read it more times than I can count. I've written this letter eleven times. This is the one I'm sending.

From March to July this year I worked on a documentary inside a long-term care home in Bedford. One of the residents was Alden Furey. You know the name. I didn't, until May.

On May 14, while I was recording an interview with him, Mr. Furey described what happened on the night of October 9, 1971. He was not being asked about it. I don't think he knew he was talking to me. He described the car, your mother, an argument, and what he and Gerard Doucette did afterward. He described where. He said she had her mother's ring on.

I have that recording. A copy is with Paul Kavanagh, a retired RCMP sergeant, and as of this week with the Halifax Regional Police historical case unit. Mr. Furey died on July 22.

I'm attaching the transcript of that part of the session. I'm not attaching the audio. If you want to hear it, I will bring it to you, wherever you are, and sit with you while you do, or leave and let you be alone with it. Whatever you want. If you never want to hear it, that is also completely yours to decide.

I'm so sorry. I'm sorry for what happened to her, and for how long you've been asking, and for being a stranger telling you this in an email. I couldn't think of a way that wasn't a wrong way.

Her name was in that room. He said it. I wanted you to know that somebody heard it.

Wren Castellanos
902-401-2277

Dear Wren,

I read it. I read it at the kitchen table and then I went and sat in the car in the driveway for an hour, I don't know why, it's where I go.

I would like to hear it. Not yet. I'll tell you when.

Thank you for writing eleven times. Thank you for the twelfth.

Maureen

P.S. Her name was Colleen Anne. Nobody ever says the Anne.

Dear Wren,

I've tried your number twice and it goes straight to a message saying it's not in service, so I'm writing here in case you still check it. Sgt. Kavanagh says you've gone to family for a while and that you're alright. I hope that's true.

I listened to it. On the 11th, in the car, in the driveway. I listened to it once and I don't think I can listen to it again but I don't need to. I know his voice now. That's a strange thing to have.

Detective Hosseini came to see me on Friday. She was kind. She said they've asked the Navy's dive unit about a survey of the Arm near the Dingle and that it isn't a no. She said not to hope. I've been not hoping for fifty-five years, I'm very good at it.

I drove to Halifax on Saturday and walked down to the water at the Dingle. It's a park. There were children. I didn't know what to do so I said her name, both names, and then I bought a coffee.

If you ever want to come and sit at my kitchen table, it's a good table. My grandmother's.

Maureen

Wren,

I know you are not reading this address, or not often, but I am writing it down so it exists somewhere.

Hosseini has formally re-opened the Mahar file as a homicide investigation. That is the first time in fifty-five years the word has been used. The Doucette vehicle was scrapped in 1979; dead end. But Doucette's widow is alive, 86, in Sydney, and she has agreed to speak. Hosseini goes up Thursday.

The break-in at your apartment has been linked in the file to the Furey correspondence. HRP will be speaking with Derek Furey this week. I would not expect him to contact you again. If he does, do not respond; send it to me.

Your witness idea is still, in my professional opinion, insane. In my personal opinion I hope it works.

Regards,
Paul Kavanagh
